title: Feature-scoped RBAC middleware for filtered usage surfaces
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: Several console usage endpoints return broad tenant-level aggregates and expose derived usage surfaces (top routes, per-token breakdowns, cost projections). Product wants feature-scoped views so teams can opt into 'billing' vs 'sensitive' metrics and to support delegated read roles (e.g., support engineer vs finance). Currently authorization is either all-or-nothing at route level which forces clients to fetch superset data and do client-side masking. This increases data blast radius and complicates Dedicated/Private deployments where tenants require stricter separation.

Goal: Implement a middleware layer for the analytics backend that applies feature-scoped RBAC at query time. The middleware should:
- Resolve caller identity and delegated roles (console token, service token, SSO group) and translate them to a consistent set of "feature authorities" (e.g., billing_read, usage_read, sensitive_metrics).
- Inject per-request row filters and projection masks into analytics queries so responses only contain permitted metrics/columns.
- Be cache-aware: include authority fingerprint in cache keys and avoid excessive cache fragmentation by using coordinated prefix caching for common authority sets.
- Support runtime feature-flag gating so we can rollout per-tenant and enable stricter policies for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Emit trace metadata for debugging and telemetry (authority resolution time, filter applied, cache hit/miss reason).

Scope: Backend middleware, query shaping hooks, unit tests, integration tests against staging analytics pipeline, migration plan for existing endpoints, and rollout plan with canary on low-traffic routes.
acceptance_criteria: Middleware resolves identity to authority set within 20ms p95 for authenticated console requests
Queries executed with injected filters return only permitted rows/columns for a matrix of roles (support, finance, admin, read-only) verified by integration tests
Cache behavior includes authority hash and does not increase memcached footprint by more than 15% in canary traffic
End-to-end latency regression <= 5% p95 on instrumented endpoints during load tests
Security review signoff and documented fallback policy when authority service is unavailable (fail-closed vs fail-open decision documented)
Feature-flag controls exist to enable/disable per-tenant and per-route; rollout runbook with rollback steps is published
comments: 2026-02-28 - Priya Nair: Kickoff meeting notes added. Product requested ability to hide 'sensitive_metrics' from support. Initial design to map SSO groups -> authority sets. Action: spike to validate query shaping approach.

2026-03-03 - Ethan Cole: Spike complete. Two options evaluated: SQL-time WHERE predicate injection vs materialized row-level views per authority. Chose predicate injection to avoid materializing many views; trade-off: requires careful index usage and predicate canonicalization.

2026-03-04 - Performance spike: baseline query 200ms median, predicate injection added +12ms median and +28ms p95 on synthetic workload for complex joins. Identified index on events(event_type, tenant_id, timestamp) reduces p95 by ~18ms.

2026-03-06 - Security review (initial): flagged requirement to ensure authority resolution is authenticated and that cache keys never leak tenant ids. Security requested a dedicated KMS-backed signing token for authority assertions.

2026-03-09 - PM feedback (Lena Ortiz): Confirmed product acceptance criteria: finance role needs aggregate export access but should not see per-user identifiers. Added requirement: column-level masking for identifiers in exports.

2026-03-10 - Ethan Cole: Implemented middleware prototype. Hooked into analytics query builder, added authority fingerprint to redis cache key, and added toggle via feature flag service. Running integration tests in staging. Next: run load test and prepare runbook for canary rollout.
